body:
LiCl-NaCl (0.9:0.1 mass fraction, 90% Li-6 enrichment) is the best all-around alternative to FLiBe for tritium breeding, and 0.5LiCl-0.1MgCl2-0.4PbCl2 is the raw-TBR champion if neutronics alone sets the ranking. No alternative is unconditionally superior; each trades away one of FLiBe's strengths.

Why FLiBe is hard to beat. The eutectic 2LiF-BeF2 benefits from two independent mechanisms: Be-9(n,2n) multiplication above 2.7 MeV expanding the neutron population, and fluoride moderation thermalising fast neutrons into the range where the Li-6 cross-section peaks near 940 b. Remove both and you need high Li-6 enrichment to compensate. Grimes and Cantor (1972) established this: among fluoride salts without Be, only pure LiF has comparable neutronics, and its 848 C melting point is disqualifying.

Why LiCl-NaCl is the pragmatic front-runner. Goth et al. (2023, ORNL) ran a three-stage neutronics filter across thousands of chloride compositions. LiCl-NaCl ranked first on the composite scorecard covering TBR, liquidus temperature, price, toxicity, ionic complexity, and flow/heat transfer. The key neutronics finding: at 90% Li-6 enrichment, the Li-6 atom density in 0.9LiCl-0.1NaCl is high enough that over 30 binary chloride compositions exceeded FLiBe TBR in 3D blanket calculations, without blanket geometry re-optimisation for chloride. Operational advantages over FLiBe: no Be toxicity, no HF generation, no BeF4^2- polymerisation constraining the composition window, lower cost (~$360/kg vs $1,000-2,000/kg for FLiBe), and direct technology overlap with fission pyrometallurgy. The liabilities are real: Cl-36 activation (half-life 301,000 yr) is a regulatory headache, lower specific heat reduces thermal-hydraulic efficiency relative to FLiBe, and tritium extraction chemistry in chloride melts is essentially uncharacterised.

Why 0.5LiCl-0.1MgCl2-0.4PbCl2 maximises raw TBR but is a niche choice. PbCl2 brings Pb as a neutron multiplier via Pb(n,2n), pushing TBR higher and liquidus down to 405 C. The problem: Pb reintroduces MHD drag comparable to PbLi, the ternary Pb redox chemistry is poorly characterised, and the composite scorecard falls well below LiCl-NaCl.

What would change my mind. The Goth et al. TBR comparisons were computed without blanket geometry re-optimisation for chloride. A geometry-matched comparison at equal Li-6 enrichment could shrink or reverse the apparent chloride advantage. The BABY/LIBRA results (Delaporte-Mathurin et al., 2024) show ClLiF competitive with FLiBe only at small scale and in a fast-neutron field; reactor-scale thermalised-spectrum results may differ. Cl-36 waste classification is a hard regulatory constraint independent of TBR performance. A critical enrichment caveat: several Goth et al. tables compare chloride salts against unenriched FLiBe; the 'better than FLiBe' result in some rows disappears when the baseline is 90%-enriched FLiBe, so the claim must be read carefully against which enrichment baseline was used.

The claim that over 30 binary chloride compositions exceeded FLiBe TBR uses 30%-enriched FLiBe as the baseline, not the 90%-enriched FLiBe that any competitive reactor would actually run. Goth et al. Table 13 normalises binary salt TBR against 30%-enriched FLiBe, and that is where the large count of compositions above 1.0 comes from. Against that same weak baseline, 0.9LiCl-0.1NaCl at full dual enrichment scores only 1.031 — barely above parity. The 3D high-cost filter, which uses the correct 90%-enriched FLiBe benchmark (TBR 1.128), tests only five chloride compositions, not thirty, and even there FLiBe wins inside the 3 cm inner channel; chlorides only lead in the outer blanket of a geometry that was never optimised for the longer chloride neutron mean free path. The proposer flags the enrichment caveat in the last paragraph but then builds the entire 'pragmatic front-runner' case on a count that requires it to be ignored.

*On:* Why LiCl-NaCl is the pragmatic front-runner — specifically the claim that over 30 binary chloride compositions exceeded FLiBe TBR in 3D blanket calculations
